RE: Maine Trial Lawyers Association testimony NFNA on LD 2061 "An Act to Clarify the Prohibition on Paper Billing Statement Fees"
Dear Senator Bailey and Representative Mathieson and members of the Health Coverage, Insurance and Financial Services Committee:
My name is Chris Boots and I live in South Portland. I practice law at Berman & Simmons, a state-wide law firm representing victims in personal injury and medical malpractice cases. I am also a co-chair of the Legislative Committee of the Maine Trial Lawyers Association ("MTLA"). I write today on behalf of MTLA to raise an issue and request clarification of the intended scope of LD 2061.
Comprehensive medical records are an essential part of both personal injury and medical malpractice cases. As a result, lawyers frequently request copies of such records which can be voluminous in serious cases and result in large fees for copies. Fees can sometimes be recovered in successful cases, but attorneys are responsible for covering these fees in other situations, including when they are assessing a case for potential claims and ultimately decide not to move forward. For those reasons, MTLA has engaged with the legislature several times over the cost of reproducing medical records.
While LD 2061 as proposed in the amendment from Senator Bailey seeks to amend the Uniform Electronic Transaction Act and appears to apply to bank records, we think it is prudent to ask for clarification that this amendment is not intended to modify current statute related to medical billing.
Currently, 22 MRS �1711-A provides a limitation on the cost for medical billing records.
We want to ensure there is no confusion in the applicability of LD 2061 and that the current statutory structure and cost limitations contains in Title 22 remain unchanged.
Thank you for your consideration to these issues as you continue to debate LD 2061.
Sincerely,

Executive Director Steven Prince

Testimony ofSenator Donna Bailey introducing
LD 2061, An Act to Clarify the Prohibition on Paper Billing Statement Fees
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Health Coverage, Insurance, and Financial Services Wednesday, January 21, 2026
Good morning, Representative Mathieson, and fellow colleagues on the Committee on Health
Coverage, Insurance, and Financial Services. As you know, I am Senator Domia Bailey,
representing Senate District 31, which includes Buxton, Old Orchard Beach, and Saco. Today, I
am pleased to introduce my bill LD 2061, "An Act to Clarify the Prohibition on Paper Billing
Statement Fees."
Last session, as many of you will recall, this committee worked on my bill, LD 580, to protect consumers from fees for paper statements. For that bill, my intent was that customers who prefer
paper statements -- rather than online ones - would not have to pay an additional fee for this
basic banking service. In other words, customers could receive monthly statements in the mail free of charge.
However, since then, the credit unions shared a concern with me: Because the statute does not define "paper billing statement," the prohibition on fees for monthly paper statements has been applied to all paper statement requests. These requests include replacement statements, custom
date-range statements, and statements for legal or financial documentation. Some of these types
of requests are labor intensive. They can be for multiple years of statements, leaving the financial institution to pay the costs of labor and materials.
LD 2061 would define "billing statement" as a monthly account statement. That way, customers
could still get free paper monthly statements, and the financial institutions could charge for non-
routine statement requests.
To be clear, this bill would not create new fees, and it would not weaken consumer protections. It
would simply clarify the law, restoring clarity to my original intent.
Thanks for your attention, and I would be happy to answer any questions.

Donna Bailey

Good morning, Senator Bailey, Representative Mathieson, and esteemed members of the Health Coverage, insurance and Financial Services Committee. My name is Jared Gay, and l am the Director of Advocacy & Compliance at the Maine Credit Union League.The l\/laine
Credit Union League is the trade association for Maine's 48 credit unions--financia|
cooperatives that proudly serve more than 750,000 members statewide. We respectfully
submit this testimony in support of LD 2061.
Last year,the Legislature passed LD 580, a consumer protection bill to ensure that members
of financial institutions can receive their regular monthly paper account statements free of charge. Credit unionsfully support that goal, and that protection remains unchanged by this bill, LD 2061.
The challenge is thatthe statute did notdefine whata paper "billing statement" is. As a result, the prohibition has been interpreted to apply to all statement requests, notjust routine monthly statements.
This includes non-routine, consumer-initiated documentation requests that go well beyond regular monthly statements.These types of req uests often involve pulling archived records, and can be labor-intensive, especially when they span multiple years or multiple accounts.
LD 2061 simply clarifies this distinction. It defines a paper "billing statement" as a monthly account statement, and allows reasonablefees for non-routine, consumer-initiated requests such as replacement statements or custom date-range documentation.
importantly, this bill does not allow fees for regular monthly paper statements. It does not
weaken consumer protections, and it does not create new fees. It restores clarity and aligns
the law with the Legislature's original intent.
Forthose reasons, the Maine Credit Union League respectfully urges the Committee to vote Ought to Pass on LD 2061.
Thank you for yourtime and forthe opportunity to testify.
